newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Bonos closed a little higher on Thursday after profit-taking eroded earlier gains made on a surprise rate cut by the Bank of Spain.
The yield curve flattened a little in the afternoon after the reduction by 25 basis points to 6.00 percent in the Spain's key money market.
"The market's expectations were for a heavy cut, so it was normal to see profit taking in the short term and people moving toward longer maturities," said a dealer in Madrid.
He added that this flattening could continue in the coming days, although a steepening should resume after that.
"But in the longer run such a modest cut in the repo rate will keep alive expectations of further cuts," said a dealer.
The long-term future contract closed up 13 bps at 114.11, and dealers said it could climb above 115 soon.
"The market traded in a range today between 114 and 114.50, but it could move higher soon above 115," said Emilio Sainz, dealer at Natwest in Madrid.
